WHEN P3-30 (PR #146) IS MERGED AND VM 108 (OR ANY REAL SERVER) IS UPDATED: RE-ENCRYPTION IS ONE WAY. Write this in the homelab log (local/homelab-changes-<date>.md) BEFORE doing it, with its undo.
What happens: the FIRST `encore update` on an install from before keys runs the OLD `encore` script: it swaps in the new compose file (the key line is tolerant: empty = the shared key), nothing is re-encrypted, logins keep working; it installs the NEW `encore` last. The SECOND `encore update`, or `sudo encore secure`, makes ENCORE_PASSWORD_KEY, takes a backup first, and restarts the music server with it: Navidrome encrypts EVERY stored password again (measured on 0.64.2, docs/evidence e08: logins keep working). It cannot be undone by putting the old compose file back: the accounts are then locked with a key the old file does not hand over and every sign-in fails (error 40) until the key is back.
Before: stop other work on that server; check `encore status`. After, do ALL of these and write the result in the log: (1) a REAL login through the app or `POST /encore/api/v1/auth/login` for the owner and one other person; (2) the backup that `secure`/`update` made first exists in /opt/encore/backups; (3) `encore secure` printed the backup key ONCE: it is saved (a password manager) and `sudo encore secure --check` accepts it; (4) the marker navidrome/.encore-password-key.sha256 exists. UNDO: `sudo encore restore <the backup made first> --key-file <key>` (it puts the old databases back; the old backup is a plain file made before the key existed: `encore restore` says so) AND copy compose.yaml.before-update back over compose.yaml if the old compose is wanted. Do NOT delete ENCORE_PASSWORD_KEY from .env at any time: all sign-ins fail until it is back.
This is the walk of P3-30 and part of P3-07 (both doors on a clean machine). Nothing here has been run on a real install yet.
